mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO falls by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 3% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases uncertainty and discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials and homebuilding equities and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a contradictory signal indicating mixed labor market dynamics, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months where PAYEMS and UNRATE move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: An above-consensus increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) relative to disposable income, sustained for two consecutive months, signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS / disposable income ratio rises for two consecutive months above historical median
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where the RSAFS/disposable income ratio rises above the historical median for two consecutive months.
